text:
B: Alright! Can you hear me?
A: Ar, I can hear you.
B: Lovely. I'm Darren.
A: Course you are. My kids' dad's a Darren. No offence.
B: Ha, none taken. There's two of us in this group, mind. I've just had the other one. Same age, same town, both got dogs. We worked out our partners both work at dentists.
A: You're having me on.
B: Hand on heart. Where are you, then?
A: Walsall.
B: Walsall. I've been to Drayton Manor, that's round your way, isn't it? Took my nephew years ago, felt sick for a week.
A: That's Tamworth, but yeah, near enough. We go when there's a deal on. I'm too old for the rides now. My back can't take it.
B: What d'you do, if you don't mind me asking?
A: Care assistant. Old people's home.
B: Fair play. That's a hard job, that. My mum's late seventies and starting to struggle a bit, and I look at the carers and think, I couldn't do it. Not properly.
A: It is hard. The pay's a joke, mind. You do personal care and hoisting all morning, and someone at head office who's never wiped a bum in their life tells you you've missed a box on a form. Do you know what I mean?
B: Ha, I do, to be fair. I run a builders' merchant, and head office sends me spreadsheets I don't look at for a week.
A: See, you're management, you'll be the one sending me the form.
B: No, no, I'm on the yard most of the time. I'd rather be on the forklift than in the office, honest.
A: Alright, I'll let you off. Do you know when this pays out, by the way? I'm still waiting on a voucher from another one.
B: No idea, mate. I didn't even read that bit, I just clicked yes.
A: Typical bloke.
B: Guilty. What do you do for fun, then, when you're not doing these?
A: Fun. Erm. Telly, mostly. Married at First Sight Australia. True crime, and then I can't sleep. And I argue with people on the Facebook group, that's my cardio.
B: Ha, my missus watches that, the Australian one. I pretend I'm not watching, then I'm asking who's with who.
A: They all do that. My brother does that. Go on, what's yours?
B: Skittles on a Thursday, in a pub team. We lost by two pins last week, I'm still not over it.
A: Skittles? Like bowling?
B: Sort of, but in a pub, with a pint, so better. And I do a barbecue every weekend in the summer. I bought a new one with my bonus. My partner says it's the most expensive thing in the house.
A: You've got bonuses? Bloody hell. We get a tin of Celebrations at Christmas.
B: Ha, it wasn't that big, to be fair.
A: Big enough for a barbecue. I'd have gone Tenerife.
